newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: G & W EXPECTS HIGHER OVERSEAS EARNINGS.
newsitem.headline: G & W EXPECTS HIGHER OVERSEAS EARNINGS.

text.p: Constuction materials and equipment supplier G & W Group (Holdings) Ltd expects higher earnings from its overseas expansion in the next few years, company officials said on Thursday.
G & W, a unit of construction firm Koh Brothers Group Ltd, said most of its income was now generated from Singapore.
"But the next few years will see more contribution from our regionalisation plans," group managing director Koh Tiak Chye told reporters during its initial public offer (IPO).
"Our overseas focus is on China, Indonesia and Malaysia, countries with healthy Gross Domestic Product forecast," said group executive director Alan Tan.
Apart from regionalisation, its expansion strategy includes upgrading of plant and equipment as well as a wider product range.
The group, which makes ready-mix concrete, precast concrete products and rents and sells equipment, has plants in the Chinese cities of Beijing and Shenyang and on the Indonesian island of Batam.
It plans to expand its precast concrete products and equipment rental and sale operations in Malaysia this year.

G & W is offering a total of 27 million new shares. The IPO comprises 10.76 million offered to the public at Singapore $0.50 each and 8.136 million preferential shares to eligible shareholders of Koh Brothers at the same price.
There will also be a placement tranche of 8.1 million offered at S$0.55 each.
It said the net proceeds of S$12.7 million from the IPO would be used to expand operations in Singapore and Malaysia.
According to its lead underwriter, United Overseas Bank Ltd, all the 8.1 million placement tranche had been fully subscribed.
G & W has forecast a 34 percent rise in its turnover for year ending December 1997 to S$130.1 million and a 23 percent rise in net profit to S$4.3 million.
